question.text: Mrs. Gupta sold her equity mutual fund units after 8 months and made a Short-Term Capital Gain of Rs. 50,000. What is the STCG tax she needs to pay?

explanation.text: The Logic: Mrs. Gupta sold the equity mutual fund units after 8 months, well inside the 12-month holding period, so the gain is Short-Term Capital Gain. Equity-oriented STCG is taxed at a flat rate of 20% (post-23 July 2024). Tax = 20% of Rs. 50,000 = Rs. 10,000. STCG does not enjoy the Rs. 1.25 lakh annual exemption that long-term equity gains do, so the entire gain is taxed. The Trap: "Rs. 7,500" applies the pre-revision 15% rate and is no longer correct. "Rs. 6,250" mistakenly applies the 12.5% LTCG rate — but this gain is short-term, not long-term. "Rs. 5,000" applies a 10% rate that is neither the current STCG nor LTCG figure. Note: The cited NISM Series V-B workbook pages (119-121) confirm the 12-month holding-period boundary and the change-of-rates from 23 July 2024 but do not explicitly state the 20% STCG rate that drives this calculation. The framing above reflects current Income Tax Act provisions as revised by Finance (No. 2) Act, 2024.
